t:
(a) 
The President is authorized to designate officers of the active list of the Marine Corps for appropriate higher commands, or for the performance of any duty of great importance and responsibility, and officers so designated may, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, have the grade, rank, pay, and allowances of lieutenant general while so serving: 
Provided, That the number of officers who may be so serving at any one time shall not exceed 10 per centum of the total authorized number of officers of the Regular Marine Corps above the grade of colonel, determined pursuant to sections 103 and 303 of this Act, made applicable to the Marine Corps by sections 114 and 314 of this Act, exclusive of those assigned to supply duty only:

Provided further, That after July 1, 1948, except in time of war or national emergency declared after the effective date of this Act, not to exceed two officers may be so serving at any one time:

Provided further, That whenever a marine officer is assigned as Chief of Staff to the President as Commander in Chief, he shall have, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, the grade, rank, pay, and allowances of general while so serving:

And provided further, That the designation of any officer as authorized by this section shall not create a vacancy in any grade of the Marine Corps nor increase the total number of officers allowed by law.

 
    (b) 
In time of war or national emergency the designations authorized by this section shall be made from officers not below the grade of colonel, and at all other times from among officers above the grade of colonel.
 
    (c) Each officer so designated shall receive the pay and allowances now or hereafter prescribed by law for the grade in which serving pursuant to this section from the date of reporting for the duty designated and until detached therefrom, at which time he shall resume his regular grade and lineal position on the active list of the Marine Corps.
 
    (d) Officers serving in the grade of lieutenant general pursuant to this section shall, while so serving, have such precedence among themselves in that grade as may be determined by the Secretary of the Navy.
 
    (e) Any officer of the Marine Corps who may be retired while serving in accordance with the provisions of this section, or subsequent to such service, may, in the discretion of the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, when retired, be placed on the retired list with the highest grade or rank held by him while on the active list: 
Provided, That no increase in retired pay shall accrue solely as the result of such advancement in rank on the retired list.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "advice and consent of the Senate" is a form of consultation before a federal decision. But the Senate is part of Congress and therefore inside the federal government, as are the President, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Marine officers being designated. The section only governs military grade, rank, pay, and retirement, with no role for states, the public, outside experts, or any other non-federal party, and no rulemaking or right to sue.
fable.s: officers so designated may, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, have the grade, rank, pay, and allowances of lieutenant general while so serving

qwen_block.w: This section describes the internal appointment and promotion of federal military officers (Marine Corps) by the President and Senate. All actors involved—the President, the Senate, and the Marine Corps officers—are inside the federal government. There is no consultation with or participation by outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_block.s: The President is authorized to designate officers of the active list of the Marine Corps for appropriate higher commands, or for the performance of any duty of great importance and responsibility, and officers so designated may, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, have the grade, rank, pay, and allowances of lieutenant general while so serving

opus.w: The only consultation in this section is the Senate's advice and consent on officer grades. The Senate is part of Congress, so the process stays inside the federal government. Everyone else involved (the President, military officers and the Secretary of the Navy) is also federal, so no outside party takes part in any decision. Words like "advice and consent" sound procedural, but nothing here crosses the federal boundary.
opus.s: officers so designated may, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, have the grade, rank, pay, and allowances of lieutenant general while so serving
opus.b: Tempting reading: the phrase "by and with the advice and consent of the Senate" sounds like consultation before a decision. It isn't participation under the definition, because the Senate is part of Congress and so sits inside the federal government. The only other actors here are the President, Marine Corps officers and the Secretary of the Navy, and all of them are federal too. No state, expert, company or member of the public takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the appointment and promotion of federal military officers. The only external interaction mentioned is the 'advice and consent of the Senate,' but the definition explicitly classifies Congress and its members as INSIDE the federal government. Since all actors involved (the President, the Senate, and the Marine Corps officers) are part of the federal government, there is no participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: The President is authorized to designate officers of the active list of the Marine Corps for appropriate higher commands, or for the performance of any duty of great importance and responsibility, and officers so designated may, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, have the grade, rank, pay, and allowances of lieutenant general while so serving
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "advice and consent of the Senate" constitutes participation because the Senate is involved in the decision. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, interaction with the Senate is intra-governmental and does not count as participation.
